title: intake
description: Stage output contract: an isolated worktree/branch was prepared and a test baseline captured.

base_sha.description: #41: the fork-point commit (worktree HEAD right after branch creation). The deterministic TEST runner diffs base_sha..worktree to classify the change (docs-only vs code).

baseline_captured.description: true only if the unit-test command actually ran at base (never fabricated)

baseline_failures.description: test ids already failing at base — inherited, not regressions; the TEST stage and the engine's regression split exclude them

baseline.description: optional human note about the captured baseline

install_skipped.description: #63: true when the dependency install was skipped because this worktree already holds a successful install of the same lockfiles

install_reason.description: #63: why install ran or was skipped (lockfile-hash-match | installed | no-lockfiles | install-failed | cache-disabled)

install_lockfiles.description: #63: lockfile names hashed for the install-cache decision

inherited_changes.description: #385: `git status --porcelain` entries the worktree ALREADY carried at intake (a reused worktree can inherit uncommitted work from a previous, dead run). Bounded: at most 20 entries plus an explicit '… (N more)' tail. Report-only — the engine never resets, stashes or adopts them.

inherited_changes_count.description: #385: the TRUE number of inherited uncommitted entries, correct even when the list above is truncated. ABSENT means unknown (the status read failed) — never assume 0.

inherited_changes_note.description: #385: which of the four honest states the read found — 'clean …', 'N uncommitted change(s) …', 'n/a (not a git worktree)' (a project setup_task may provision a non-git worktree), or 'unreadable: <reason>'. An unreadable tree must never read as a clean one.
